narrative:
The model determined that you have a 58% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and your property ownership situation. Your checking account status was the most important reason for the denial. Having a negative balance pushes the prediction quite strongly toward bad credit risk, especially since only 12.6% of approved applicants are in this situation while most have either no checking account or positive balances.

The requested loan duration worked in your favor. At 12 months it is considerably shorter than the 19-month average among approved loans, which helped pull the prediction back toward approval. However, this positive effect was not large enough to overcome the other factors.

Your lack of property was the third most influential element and again pushed the decision toward denial. Having no identifiable assets puts you in a small minority compared with approved applicants, most of whom own a car, real estate, or insurance policies.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude the risk was too high. To improve your chances on a future application, focus first on bringing your checking account into positive territory and, if possible, acquiring a tangible asset that can serve as collateral. Once those areas are stronger, you may wish to reapply.
